title: Meta built a virtual brain that can predict virality before it happens #shorts
description:
Meta just built a digital brain that can actually predict virality.

It’s called Tribe v2.

And this is gonna be a content cheat code for the people that figure out how to use it.

Tribe was built using real MRI brain scans from over 700 people.

The participants watched videos, listened to podcasts, read articles…and the MRIs recorded which parts of their brain got activated.

But here’s the crazy part…

Meta then took that data and mapped it across 70,000 different points in the brain to create a digital version.

Essentially, a cloned virtual brain that can simulate different responses.

Showing faces caused one reaction, while sharing emotional words caused another.

And this is where it gets interesting…

When you feed a piece of content into the Tribe model, it will give you a prediction for where the brain will be activated.

And it turns out Tribe v2 is way better at this prediction than literally any other scan on Earth.

So you can imagine how powerful this is…

When you feed a piece of content in, if the dopamine reward centers in the brain light up, you’ve likely got a viral banger on your hands.

It’s a neural engine for predicting attention.

The beauty of this is that Tribe isn’t really based on video data performance.

Instead, it’s reverse engineering what the human brain will literally do.

Now tribe v2 is completely free and publicly accessible.

So whoever figures out how to tap into this for content, is going to have a huge advantage.

If you want me to send you the link to their paper and model, comment “Tribe” and I’ll send it through.
